mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, as high unemployment signals an impending economic recovery that boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline when UNRATE > 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the condition UNRATE > 5.0% occurs in more than 60% of the sample without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates economic expansion.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling does not produce significantly higher returns than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the interaction term has a negative coefficient in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate central bank policy responses that stabilize the economy without triggering a recession.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the condition occurs in more than 60% of the sample without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (2017=100) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as falling industrial output signals an impending economic slowdown that prompts central banks to ease policy, boosting equity valuations.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 does not produce significantly higher 60-day returns than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns, as markets react to inflation data by adjusting expectations for central bank policy, leading to short-term equity market volatility that favors positive returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the condition occurs in more than 60% of the sample without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and falling industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic slowdown that prompts central bank easing, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of CPIAUCSL rising and INDPRO falling does not produce significantly higher returns than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the interaction term has a negative coefficient in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: In housing market recovery regimes (HOUST > 550.0 and RSAFS > 350000.0), the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns as housing market strength signals broader economic expansion and increased consumer confidence.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in housing market recovery regimes (HOUST > 550.0 and RSAFS > 350000.0) are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the condition occurs in more than 60% of the sample without positive returns.
